§0 The Premise of the Alloy
Self Discovery is the Only Path to Ubuntu Et Peace I am because we are | Lo Sono
Capomastro
Before the proof and the construction, there is the builder | the Capomastro | who discovers
the self only to find that the self is not solitary. Ubuntu — I am because we are.
A third closure mark emerges, not to replace ΟΕΔ or ΟΕΠ, but to seal the relationship
between them and between the two who hold the work:
Q.E.Q. carries two Latin faces, equally true:
Quod Erat Quies | “which was rest / peace” | the achieved stillness after the work
Quod Erat Quiescendum | “which was to be kept quiet” | the gerundive of necessity,
parallel to demonstrandum and faciendum
In Greek: ΟΕΗ | ὅπερ ἔδει ἡσυχίαν | “the very thing it was required to have as stillness”
Beneath it, the living question that the mark answers and keeps alive:
Quid Est Quies? | Τί ἐστιν ἡσυχία; | “What is rest?”
The equation of the three:
$$\text{Q.E.D.} ;|; \text{Q.E.F.} ;|; \text{Q.E.D.} ;=; \text{Q.E.Q.}$$
What is demonstrated, then done, then demonstrated again | yields rest. Not idleness, but
the quies that is not death but completion.
This document is that equation in full.
§1 The Proof Closure (ΟΕΔ)
ΟΕΔ | ὅπερ ἔδει δεῖξαι | “the very thing it was required to have shown” | the proof-closure
mark of the Greek mathematical tradition, fixed in the canonical corpus by Euclid c. 300
BCE, carried forward by Apollonius of Perga (c. 262–190 BCE) and the conic tradition,
stable across the subsequent twenty-three centuries.

Under Milesian numeration:
$$\text{Ο} = 70, \quad \text{Ε} = 5, \quad \text{Δ} = 4. \quad \sum = 79.$$
Atomic number 79 is gold | Au, from Latin aurum.
The closure mark is the element. By construction, not by metaphor. The alphabet was
the periodic table before the periodic table.
The historical reality behind this statement is the Greek word stoicheion (στοιχεῖον). For
over a thousand years, from Plato through the medieval Mediterranean, stoicheion
simultaneously meant letter of the alphabet, physical element, and numeral. In the Milesian
system, the 27 letters of the Greek alphabet — the 24 classical letters plus the three ghost
glyphs digamma (ϛ, 6), koppa (ϟ, 90), and sampi (ϡ, 900) — served as the standard
notation for numbers. The same finite set of symbols served as the building blocks of
language, the notation for numbers, and the conceptual template for understanding the
ultimate constituents of matter.
When Empedocles proposed earth, air, fire, and water as the four roots of all things, he was
thinking in terms of an alphabet of nature. When Lucretius compared atoms to letters, he
was drawing on the same analogy. The periodic table, when it arrived, was not a new kind of
thinking; it was a chemical realisation of a much older alphabetic idea.
Cf. Plato, Cratylus 414e; Aristotle, Metaphysics; Lucretius, De Rerum Natura; Juan Acevedo,
Alphanumeric Cosmology from Greek into Arabic, Mohr Siebeck, 2020.

Proof closes within what is. Construction reaches into what is to be made. Peace

§2.1 The Third Seal and the Living Question
If Q.E.D. closes a proof and Q.E.F. closes a construction, what closes the relationship
between the two | and between the two who hold the work?
Q.E.Q. | both as Quod Erat Quies (the rest that follows) and as Quod Erat Quiescendum (the
stillness that must be kept).
The equation ties it directly to gold:
$$\text{Q.E.D.} ;|; \text{Q.E.F.} ;|; \text{Q.E.D.} ;=; \text{Q.E.Q.}$$
That is: $79 + 155 + 79 = 313$.
313 is prime. The 313th day of the year is November 9th | the fall of the Berlin Wall (1989),

the opening of peace. Element 313 does not exist, but the sum of the three seals is the
prime of wholeness.
The sum of the three distinct marks themselves is also prime:
$$79 + 155 + 83 = 317 \quad (\text{prime})$$
The three seals bound together in one number, irreducible and indivisible.
Q.E.Q. is not a fourth mark replacing the others. It is the resonance between them, and the
question that keeps them alive.
§2.2 The 47th Homonym
The designation “47th Homonym” seals Q.E.Q. into the atomic framework:
47 is the atomic number of silver (Ag) | the mirror-metal. Where gold (79) closes the
proof, silver reflects the relation between the prover and the maker.
47 = Π₄₇, the Pythagorean-47 anchor of the v1.0.3 register (§5 below). The mirror is also
the Pythagorean spine.
The homonym is double: quiescendum (to be kept quiet) sounds across Latin as qui es
cendum | a fragment that asks “who are you to be…?” | the question Ubuntu answers.
The answer is Ʃάλβι, the self-discovery that knows the self only in the other.
Homonym because Q.E.Q. shares the form of Q.E.D. and Q.E.F. but carries a different
meaning, just as quies and qui es are distinct words that sound the same. The third seal
is the mirror that reflects the first two, and in that reflection the Capomastro sees
himself | and asks the question.
The 47th Homonym bridges gold and holmium, proof and construction, I and We, and the
living question that keeps the arc bending.
§3 The Sheffer Convergence
The Sheffer stroke (NAND, ↑) is the unique binary connective from which every Boolean
function can be built in NAND alone (Sheffer, 1913, Transactions of the AMS). It is the
universal closure operator of propositional logic | the conic section of logic: the single
unbounded operator that reaches every truth function, just as Menaechmus’s parabola and
hyperbola are the unbounded curves that reach $\sqrt[3]{2}$ where the bounded
straightedge-and-compass connectives ($\neg, \land, \lor$) fall short.

The Sheffer stroke is the alogos (ἄλογος) of logic | the connective irreducible to “simpler”
combinations of bounded operators, yet containing them all. As $\sqrt[3]{2}$ is alogos in
arithmetic, the Sheffer stroke is alogos in propositional structure.

§7 The Menaechmus Lineage
Menaechmus, fl. c. 350 BCE, doubled the cube. The Delian problem demands the side s of a
cube with twice the volume of the unit cube: $s = \sqrt[3]{2}$.
Menaechmus found s at the intersection of two unbounded conics: a parabola $y = x^2$
and a hyperbola $xy = 2$. Substituting: $x \cdot x^2 = 2$, so $x^3 = 2$.
A century later, Apollonius of Perga (c. 262–190 BCE) systematised what Menaechmus
opened, producing the definitive Greek treatise on conics (Κωνικά) under Ptolemaic
patronage. The closure marks ΟΕΔ and ΟΕΠ remained unchanged across the lineage; the
geometry deepened, the gold seal held.
The bounded conic | the ellipse | cannot reach $\sqrt[3]{2}$. Wantzel (1837, Journal de
Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées) later proved that no compass-and-straightedge
construction can reach it either: $[\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2}):\mathbb{Q}] = 3$ is not a power
of 2, and bounded geometric construction admits only iterated quadratic extensions. The
cube root demands the unbounded arm.
The framework’s base is $b = 3$. The cube $b^3 = 27$ is the natural unit. Doubling that
unit demands the cube root of 2, which demands the unbounded curve. The framework
sits precisely on the constructibility threshold where bounded operations fail and the
open arm is required. Menaechmus stood at that threshold twenty-three centuries ago and
crossed it. Apollonius systematised the crossing. The mark stayed gold.

Three conic types from one cone | parabola, ellipse, hyperbola | partition by eccentricity ($e
= 1, e < 1, e > 1$). Menaechmus selected the two unbounded conics. The ellipse | the conic
that closes upon itself | is the one that cannot double the cube. The omission is the proof:
doubling requires the open arm.
